questions.question: In which state of India is shifting cultivation known as Bringa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the state of **Odisha**, **shifting cultivation** is referred to as **Bringa**.
 
• This form of agriculture involves **clearing a piece of land by cutting down and burning the vegetation**, then using the cleared land for cultivation.
 
• Shifting cultivation is a traditional practice among various indigenous communities in Odisha.
 
• It is primarily practiced in the hilly and forested regions of the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shifting cultivation**, also known as** slash-and-burn agriculture**, is a method where farmers rotate the fields they cultivate rather than farming the same land continuously.
 
• This practice helps in maintaining soil fertility and controlling pests and weeds naturally.
 
• However, it can **lead to deforestation and soil erosion** if not managed sustainably.
 
• Efforts are being made to introduce more sustainable agricultural practices among the communities practicing shifting cultivation.

questions.question: In which type of farming the land is used for growing food and fodder crops and rearing livestock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Mixed farming.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mixed farming:-**

 
 
• It is a type of agriculture that combines the production of crops and livestock on the same farm.
 
• **The type of farming in which the land is used for growing food and fodder crops and rearing livestock is called mixed farming. (Hence option 2 is correct)**
 
• It is a sustainable and efficient system that can provide a variety of benefits, including:
 
 
• **Increased income and productivity**: Mixed farms can generate income from both crop and livestock sales, and the two enterprises can often complement each other. For example, the manure produced by livestock can be used to fertilize crops, and the crops can provide feed for the livestock.
 
• **Improved soil health: **Mixed farming can help to improve soil health by rotating crops and using manure to fertilize the land. This can lead to increased crop yields and reduced erosion.
 
• **Reduced risk**: Mixed farming can help to reduce risk by diversifying the farm's income streams. If one enterprise fails, the other can help to support the farm.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plantation agriculture:-**

 
 
• **Plantation agriculture is a type of commercial farming in which a single crop is grown on a large scale. **
 
• Plantations are typically owned by a single company or government, and they employ labourers to work on the land.
 
 
 
• **Subsistence farming:-**
 
 
• **It is a type of agriculture in which farmers grow crops and raise livestock to meet their own needs and the needs of their families, with little or no surplus for sale. **
 
• Subsistence farming is practiced all over the world, but it is particularly common in developing countries.
 
 
 
• **Shifting cultivation:-**
 
 
• **It is a type of agriculture in which plots of land are cultivated temporarily, then abandoned while post-disturbance fallow vegetation is allowed to freely grow while the cultivator moves on to another plot. **
 
• The period of cultivation is usually terminated when the soil shows signs of exhaustion or, more commonly, when the field is overrun by weeds.
 
• The period of time during which the field is cultivated is usually shorter than the period over which the land is allowed to regenerate by lying fallow.

questions.question: ______ is also known as industrial agriculture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Intensive farming.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• An intensive type of farming is practised in areas of high population pressure on land.
 
• **Intensive farming or intensive agriculture** also known as **industrial agriculture** is characterized by a **low fallow ratio** and higher use of inputs such as **capital and labour per unit of land area.**
 
• This is in **contrast to traditional agriculture** in which the **inputs per unit of land are lower**.
 
• It is labour-intensive farming, where high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation are used for obtaining higher production.
 
• Intensive subsistence farming yields two types of crops- wet and dry.
 
• While the wet crops include paddy, the dry ones vary from wheat, pulses, maize, and millets, to sorghum, soya beans, tubers, and vegetables.
 
• Extensive farming is done in those countries where the landholding size is large e.g. the United States, Canada, etc.
 
• Extensive farming is almost absent in India except in a few states such as **Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__** Subsistence farming

 
• Subsistence agriculture is practised on small patches of land with the help of primitive tools like hoe, dao and digging sticks, and family/community labour.
 
• This type of farming depends upon monsoon, natural fertility of the soil and suitability of other environmental conditions for the crops grown.

Plantation Farming

 
• Plantation Farming is farming in an estate where a single cash crop is grown for sale.
 
• Examples are **Tea, Coffee, Rubber, Bananas, and Spices.**

Shifting cultivation

 
• ​Shifting cultivation is a form of agricultural practice in which farmers clear an area of land by slashing vegetation and burning forests for agricultural purposes.
 
• Shifting cultivation is a mode of farming long followed in the humid tropics.
 
• This is the practice of planting crops in the exposed, ash-fertilized soil for two or three seasons in succession. 
 
• As the original organic matter reserve in the topsoil decomposed and as the high rainfall would leach out the nutrients from the root zone, the farmers would abandon the cleared plot and move to an adjacent patch of forest.
 
• This practice is also known as slash-and-burn agriculture or slash-and-burn cultivation.

questions.question: In which type of farming, the land is used for growing food and fodder crops and rearing livestock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mixed farming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mixed farming** is a type of farming where the land is used for both **growing food and fodder crops as well as rearing livestock.**
 
• It involves a** combination of crop production and animal husbandry**.
 
• In **mixed farming systems, farmers grow crops such as wheat, maize, vegetables, fruits, etc., for food production, while also keeping livestock like cattle, sheep, goats, or poultry for meat, milk, eggs, and other by-products.**
 
• This type of farming allows farmers to have a diversified income stream and optimize the use of available resources by** integrating crop and animal production.**

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dairy farming:**

 
 
• Dairy farming is a type of farming focused on the production of milk and milk products.
 
• It involves raising dairy animals, typically cows, but also goats or sheep, to obtain milk that can be processed into various products such as butter, cheese, yogurt, and ice cream. 
 
 
 
• **Plantation farming: **
 
 
• Plantation farming is a type of farming that involves the large-scale cultivation of a single crop, typically cash crops such as tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane, palm oil, or bananas.
 
• It is commonly practiced in tropical or subtropical regions with favorable climate conditions for the specific crop. 
 
 
 
• **Commercial farming:**
 
 
• Commercial farming refers to agricultural practices that focus on producing crops or livestock for sale in the market, with the primary goal of generating profit.
 
• It typically involves large-scale production and the use of modern technologies, machinery, and inputs such as fertilizers and pesticides.

questions.question: In which of the following groups of States and Union Territories is 'slash and burn' agriculture known as 'Dipa'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh and Andaman & Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Slash and burn' agriculture is known as 'Dipa' in the tribal regions of **Chhattisgarh and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.**
 
• 'Dipa' is a traditional form of agriculture practiced by indigenous communities where forests are cleared and burned for farming.
 
• This method is primarily used for cultivating crops like rice, millets, and vegetables in these regions.
 
• The practice is prevalent among tribal communities due to its simplicity and adaptation to local environmental conditions.
 
• While it serves as a subsistence farming method, it has ecological implications such as deforestation and soil degradation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slash and Burn Agriculture:**

 
 
• Also known as shifting cultivation, it involves clearing vegetation and burning it to enrich the soil with nutrients.
 
• Commonly practiced in tropical regions around the world.
 
• The method is often unsustainable due to soil erosion and biodiversity loss.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Impact:**
 
 
• Deforestation leads to loss of wildlife habitats and carbon sequestration capacity.
 
• Burning vegetation releases greenhouse gases, contributing to climate change.
 
• Soil fertility declines after repeated cycles, leading to abandonment of the land.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Sustainable Practices:**
 
 
• Agroforestry integrates crops and trees to maintain soil fertility.
 
• Crop rotation helps preserve soil nutrients and reduce pest risks.
 
• Terrace farming prevents soil erosion in hilly areas.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Slash and burn agriculture is practiced under different names worldwide, such as 'Milpa' in Central America and 'Kaingin' in the Philippines.
 
• Efforts are being made internationally to replace it with more sustainable farming methods.

questions.question: Which of the following types of agriculture is known as Jhum in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shifting Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shifting Agriculture**

 
 
• Under Shifting cultivation, a piece of land is used for quite some years until the fertility is dropped. After that, the farmers move to the new plots. It is practiced by tribal and is also known as Burn and Slash cultivation.
 
• It is known as Jhoom in Assam, Bewar in Madhya Pradesh, Onam in Kerala, Podu in Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha.
 
• 
 
Over a large part of North East India shifting cultivation used, while having different local names are found to be the same-named as Jhoom cultivation. Jhoom cultivation, also known as Slash-and-Burn cultivation.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Other Names of Shifting Cultivation:

__
 
• Shifting Cultivation is known as Ladang in Indonesia,__
 
• Caingin in the Philippines,
 
• Milpa in Central America & Mexico,
 
• Ray in Vietnam,
 
• Taungya in Myanmar,
 
• Tamrai in Thailand,
 
• __Chena in Sri Lanka,__
 
• Conuco in Venezuela,
 
• Roca in Brazil,
 
• Masole in central Africa.

questions.question: According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 2022-23, which state of India is the largest producer of sugarcane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of sugarcane in India, according to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 2022-23.
 
• It contributes approximately 38% of the total sugarcane production in the country.
 
• The state has a favorable climate and fertile soil, which are ideal for sugarcane cultivation.
 
• The major sugarcane-producing regions in Uttar Pradesh include Western and Central parts of the state.
 
• Uttar Pradesh also has a significant number of sugar mills, aiding in the production and processing of sugarcane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sugarcane Varieties**

 
 
• Different varieties of sugarcane are grown in India, including Co 0238, Co 86032, and Co 0118, which are known for their high yield and sugar content.
 
• These varieties are developed by various agricultural research institutes to improve productivity and disease resistance.
 
 
 
• **Sugarcane By-products**
 
 
• By-products of sugarcane include molasses, bagasse, and press mud.
 
• Molasses is used in the production of ethanol, bagasse is used as a biofuel, and press mud is used as a soil amendment.
 
 
 
• **Sugarcane Processing**
 
 
• Sugarcane processing involves crushing the cane to extract juice, which is then boiled to produce sugar crystals.
 
• The process also involves clarification, evaporation, crystallization, and centrifugation.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact**
 
 
• Sugarcane farming is a significant source of income for millions of farmers in India.
 
• The sugar industry contributes substantially to the rural economy and employment.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives**
 
 
• The Indian government supports sugarcane farmers through various schemes, including subsidies and minimum support prices.
 
• Research and development initiatives are undertaken to improve crop yield and sustainability.

questions.question: "Agricultural Census" is conducted in India at an interval of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __5 Years.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Agriculture Census forms part of a broader system of collection of Agricultural Statistics.
 
• It is a large-scale statistical operation for the collection and derivation of quantitative information about the structure of agriculture.
 
• Agricultural Census is the main source of information on a variety of agricultural parameters at a relatively minute level
 
• Through Agriculture Census it is endeavoured to collect basic data on important aspects of the agricultural economy for all the operational holdings in the country. 
 
• It collects data such as
 
 
• Number and area of ​​operational holdings,
 
• Farm size,
 
• Class-wise distribution,
 
• Land use,
 
• Tenancy,
 
• Cropping pattern
 
• Use of fertilizers, insecticides etc.,
 
 
 
• The Agriculture Census in India is conducted at an interval of five years following broad guidelines of the decennial World Census of Agriculture (WCA) evolved by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations.
 
• Entire Census operation is conducted in three phases
 
• Operational holding is taken as a statistical unit at micro level for data collection.
 
• The aggregation of data is done at various levels of administrative units.
 
• India's first ever comprehensive Agricultural Census was carried out with the agricultural year 1970-71 as the reference

questions.question: The word agriculture is derived from the Latin words ager and culture. What does ‘ager’ mean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agriculture**

 
 
• Agriculture can be defined as the **art **and **science** of cultivating crops and rearing livestock for man use.
 
• It is a science because it involves the use of scientific methods for the production of both plants and animals it equally involves the application of scientific and technological knowledge.
 
 
 
• Soil
 
 
• Plants obtain inorganic elements from the soil, which serves as a natural medium for land plants. 
 
• Soil is the outer loose layer that covers the surface of Earth.
 
• Soil quality is a major determinant, along with climate, of plant distribution and growth.
 
• Soil quality depends not only on the chemical composition of the soil but also on the topography (regional surface features) and the presence of living organisms.
 
• In agriculture, the history of the soil, such as the cultivating practices and previous crops, modify the characteristics and fertility of that soil.
 
• Soil develops very slowly over long periods of time, and its formation results from natural and environmental forces acting on minerals, rock, and organic compounds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rocks**

 
 
• The earth's crust is made up of various types of rocks, differing from one another in texture, structure, colour, permeability, mode of occurrence, and degree of resistance to denudation.
